label: Supabase
summary: A hosted database with sign-in built in. You create a free account on their website; there is nothing to install or run on your computer.
fits: an app that needs accounts or saved information and has nobody to look after a server.

env.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL
env.what: the address of your Supabase project (Project URL)

env.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY
env.what: the publishable key, which starts with sb_publishable_
env.where: Supabase dashboard > your project > Connect, or Settings > API Keys

steps: Open https://supabase.com/dashboard/new/_ in your browser. Sign in, or create a free account first.

Fill in the new-project form: a project name, a database password (save it in a password manager; it is not one of the two values below), and the region closest to your users. Create the project and wait until it is ready.
On the project page, click "Connect" at the top. The dialog shows the Project URL and the publishable key for the framework you select; choose Next.js.
Copy the Project URL. In the env file named below, replace the placeholder after NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL= with it.
Copy the publishable key (it starts with sb_publishable_). Replace the placeholder after NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY= with it. Every key is also listed under Settings > API Keys.
Do not put a secret key (it starts with sb_secret_) or the legacy service_role key in this file: those are for servers only and must never reach a browser.
Save the file, then start the app again (pnpm dev) so it reads the new values.

drifts: where the dashboard shows the URL and the key (the Connect dialog, Settings > API Keys)
the legacy anon / service_role keys: Supabase states they are deprecated by the end of 2026
